lines.n: The trampled snow on the road into the village is speckled brown and black. Elain and Nesta came the moment they saw the hides in her satchel.

do.text: Sell the hides in the market square. Then head home by the east road.

lines.t: May the Immortal Light shine upon thee, sisters. Have you a moment to hear the Word of the Blessed?
No. We don't.

lines.n: Nesta pushes back her sleeve to show the iron bracelet on her wrist. The acolyte gasps.

lines.t: This is what you should be wearing. Not some silver bells to attract those faerie monsters.
Prythian is a land of peace and plenty. Our benevolent masters would never harm us.
You're fighting an uphill battle.
A worthy cause.
No, it's not.
Remember what I said, girl. Stay out of the deep woods.
I don't barter goods for my services. I only accept coin.
I have a wolf pelt and a doe hide for sale. I hunted them myself. I swear it.
You weren't lying about the wolf's size. Doesn't seem like a faerie, though.

lines.n: She names her price. She is overpaying, by a lot.

lines.t: Someone once did the same for me and mine. Figure it's time to repay what's due.
A word of advice, from one hunter to another. Don't go far into the woods. More and more of those things are slipping through the wall.
A nobleman I guarded heard a pack of martax crossed in the night. Body big as a bear's, head like a lion's, three rows of teeth. Half a village in ribbons.

do.text: Spend your coin if you like (charm stall). Then take the east road home.

lines.n: A stall of charms, baubles, incantations and bits of iron, catering to the village's fears.
The weathered cobbler pretends not to watch her satchel. His usual offers are an insult.
Isaac is long gone down the road.
Isaac Hale leans against a building across the square, arms crossed. He inclines his head in a familiar gesture, then ambles off toward the old barn outside town.

lines.t: I do hope you two are taking precautions.

lines.n: No love, never had been. Just a release, a reprieve, a bit of selfishness.

do.text: Later, the light outside the barn has turned long and gray.

lines.t: He's going to marry some Greenfield girl with a handsome dowry anyway.
I'll find something for Father. I promise.
Feyre … the spice stall smells like the old house.

choices.t: Press a twenty-mark copper into her palm. (Canon, -5 coin)

lines.t: Are you going to sell them, Feyre? The mercenary keeps looking over.
I'll see you at home.

lines.n: That evening Elain brings back a new chisel for their father's carving. Nesta chops wood a second time without being asked.

lines.t: Of course. You're right.
Not until the hides are sold.

lines.n: Later, after another dinner of venison, they gather around the fire for the quiet hour before bed. Father dozes, his cane across his knee.
